ev.q: During 2021–2022, the estimated age-adjusted COVID-19–associated death rate decreased 47%, from 115.6 to 61.3 per 100,000 persons.
In 2022, COVID-19 was listed as an underlying or contributing cause of 244,986 (61.3 per 100,000) deaths
In 2022, among deaths with COVID-19 listed on the death certificate, COVID-19 was listed as the underlying cause in 76% of deaths
approximately 59% of COVID-19–associated deaths occurred in a hospital inpatient setting, followed by 15% in the decedent’s home
COVID-19 deaths that listed additional causes of death included an average of 4.5 listed contributing causes, compared with 4.2 in 2021 and 4.0 in 2020.
The COVID-19–associated age-adjusted death rate varied by HHS region, with the lowest rates in New England (Region 1) and highest rates in the south central United States (Region 6).
Age-adjusted death rates were calculated by sex, race and ethnicity, and residence.
This report summarizes provisional U.S. COVID-19 death data for 2022.
The percentage of deaths occurring in a hospital inpatient setting decreased from nearly 70% during 2020–2021 to approximately 60% in 2022.

methods_quotes.q: Age-adjusted death rates were calculated by sex, race and ethnicity, and residence. Crude death rates were calculated by age.
The population data used to calculate deaths rates are July 1, 2021 estimates, based on the Blended Base produced by the U.S. Census Bureau
Place of death is noted on the death certificate and is determined by both the location where the death was pronounced and the physical location where the death occurred
